programme: VDR, HMGA2 and PLAGL2 converge on IGF/PI3K-AKT growth-and-survival signaling: HMGA2 is a chromatin-architectural driver whose own target list includes IGF1, IGF2BP2, AKT1 and KRAS; PLAGL2 drives proliferation through IGF2 (documented as a Wnt-independent, ASCL2/IGF2-mediated mechanism); VDR sits upstream of the same AKT/mitochondrial node, its ligand (calcitriol/vitamin D3) modulating AKT-dependent survival and proliferation in both a Drosophila neuronal model and colorectal tumor cells.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease this axis governs neuronal survival and mitochondrial function: VDR signaling supports neuronal/mitochondrial dynamics and attenuates amyloid pathology, while the miR-132/HMGA2 arm of the same PI3K/AKT pathway is protective in a mouse AD model — loss of HMGA2 regulation or VDR tone would erode AKT-dependent neuroprotection.
role_in_b: In colorectal cancer the same axis runs in the growth-promoting direction: HMGA2 transcriptionally supports IGF1/IGF2BP2/AKT1/KRAS-driven proliferation and EMT, PLAGL2 drives IGF2-dependent, Wnt-independent tumor growth, and VDR/calcitriol signaling opposes this proliferative program, consistent with its association with better prognosis.
shared_axis: IGF-PI3K-AKT signaling is a growth/survival axis used by both tissues for opposite ends — neuronal maintenance in brain, proliferation control in colon epithelium — so a network built around VDR, HMGA2 and PLAGL2 recurs in both diseases because it recurs wherever this axis is dysregulated, not because the diseases are otherwise linked.
reasoning: VDR and HMGA2 each have direct primary-literature placement in both Alzheimer's disease and colorectal cancer, and PLAGL2 has direct CRC evidence naming the IGF2 mechanism, so the module is nameable and well-grounded per factor; but no retrieved paper documents the two diseases sharing this axis together — the bridge is inferred from the fact that each disease separately implicates the same PI3K/AKT node, not from anything stated about the pair.
support: 41335161 (VDR ortholog modulates neuronal and mitochondrial dynamics in a Drosophila AD model — places VDR in AD); 41910814 (Vitamin D3 attenuates AD-like pathology via amyloid remodeling — VDR/AD); 39112893 (VDR genotype affects rivastigmine response in Iranian AD patients — VDR/AD, genetic); 42203331 (calcitriol/VDR anti-tumor action in colorectal cancer — VDR/CRC); 41987077 (circulating vitamin D status and CRC prognosis, systematic review — VDR/CRC); 34150043 (miR-132/HMGA2/PI3K-AKT axis protective in AD mouse model — HMGA2/AD); 40518465 (HMGA2 highly expressed across tumor types including colon — HMGA2/CRC); 32699331 (gene co-expression biomarker study places PLAGL2 in AD staging; does not itself discuss CRC, so this is AD-only evidence despite the reader's note); 38500386 (PLAGL2 marker of mucinous colorectal cancer with MUC2 — PLAGL2/CRC); 37310750 (PLAGL2 drives CRC via ASCL2/IGF2, Wnt-independent mechanism — PLAGL2/CRC, names the IGF axis).
how_to_falsify: In parallel VDR-deficient/vitamin-D-depleted models — an AD neuronal model (e.g. APP/PS1 mice or patient iPSC-neurons) and a colorectal organoid or xenograft — knock down HMGA2 and PLAGL2 and measure AKT phosphorylation and IGF1/IGF2 pathway output alongside the disease phenotype (amyloid burden vs. proliferation/tumor growth); if VDR status fails to modulate HMGA2/PLAGL2-driven AKT signaling in either tissue, or if the phenotypic readouts move independently of pathway activity, the shared-axis account is wrong.
caveats: Brain and colorectal tissue have no established direct comorbidity pathway in clinical practice, so this is a mechanistic-overlap claim, not a stated disease link. 152 patient-group comparisons across 6 independent cohort pairs give solid recurrence for VDR and HMGA2 (126/152 and 116/152) but weaker recurrence for PLAGL2 (102/152), so the IGF2-specific PLAGL2 contribution should be weighted less. The single-view exclusions (SALL1, IRF6, RCOR1, TCF7L1, GFI1B, LCOR, BATF, SOX11) confirm the account is not built on one outlier subgroup. The tissue-generic exclusions (TAL1, EGR4, HDAC7, RFX5, STAT4, NR3C1, ZEB1, SOX10, NOTCH1) removed canonical EMT/hematopoietic master regulators — their absence is why this account does not reach for an EMT master-TF explanation instead. Roughly half the surviving factors (HOXB3, ZNF451, PAX9, SMARCC1, ZBTB18) and three more with CRC-only evidence (FOXA2, TP53, FOSL1, SOX7) are deliberately excluded from the carrying set because this record places them, at best, in only one of the two diseases or in neither.
